National Parliament
National Assembly
Twenty-First Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
2083 Ashadh 4 - Friday
Meeting No. 19
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:19 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members,
(13:19 hrs)
Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. A time limit of 1 minute each has been set for speaking in the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina.
Honourable Mr. Goma Devi Timalsina
(13:20 hrs)
(Nepali Communist Party):- Mr. Chairperson, I seek permission to raise a few points during today's Zero Hour.
The government never tires of talking about good governance. The government's policy is only to trouble the poor and helpless citizens. Squatters' houses have been demolished, and they have been made destitute. Squatters kept in holding centers are not even getting food, medicine, or water. Women, the elderly, and children are in distress. How long will this government keep them suffering like this? The government's representatives must answer here. Students have not been able to study yet. Where to study, where to eat, where to live? There is no certainty. Seven people have already died. Squatters from 27 places have been removed. Among these, 28 (..time ended.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
(13:21 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, compared to yesterday, incidents of violence against women, murder, and rape are increasing day by day. Just on Jestha 28th, in Achham District, Tharkari Rural Municipality Ward No. 4, a ward member passed away due to illness. Afterwards, when Dharamraj Saud was sent to fetch medicine for his relatives, some local individuals defamed him, insulted him, and harassed him by taking various photos and spreading them on social media. Not only that, but they also physically assaulted him. Therefore, the criminals involved should be thoroughly studied, investigated, and brought under the purview of legal action. Similarly, many incidents have occurred in this period, such as the case of Ishree Bhujel by her husband and the incident in Kailali where Dhamadevi's tempo was overturned. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Durga Gurung.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:22 hrs)
After the budget was made public, ward residents and representatives have called repeatedly, saying, "The projects we expected were not included." I want to ask the government: why are the real needs of the people and the projects proposed by the local levels ignored? If the development projects expected by the citizens in villages are not included in the budget, but projects are selected based on influence and connections, where will the people find justice? I want to tell the government that the spirit of federalism is to formulate projects according to the needs of the people, but today, instead of listening to the priorities of the local levels, a tendency to impose decisions from the center is evident. I want a clear answer from the Finance Minister: what is more important, the needs of the people or the influence of the connected? Not discrimination in the name of development, but equal opportunity and equitable budget distribution. (..time ended.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
(13:23 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:24 hrs)
Just yesterday, the team led by the Chief of the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority was summoned to the Prime Minister's Office, detained for about 9 hours, verbally abused, and then the Director of the Department of Passports and the Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs were summoned, and the Director of the Department of Passports was arrested on the spot. Is this government ruling by law or by anarchy? Furthermore, a foreign diplomatic head was summoned, and the Prime Minister's Office's henchmen intimidated him. The country is being disgraced diplomatically. Therefore, I want to say that this government, which is trying to rule by self-immolation, will not last long. So, it should not make such mistakes.
Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:25 hrs)
Sir, Kailali district has the largest number of freed Kamaiyas in the country. Especially among Banke, Bardiya, Dadeldhura, Kanchanpur, and Kailali, Kailali is not just the district with the highest number. The government has even managed large settlements of freed Kamaiyas. In those remote villages, apart from the two, three, or five katthas of land provided by the government, there is no other employment arrangement, forcing the youth to work in risky fishing jobs in Maharashtra, India, for minimum wages.
This is an issue I have raised in Parliament before. If cottage industries that require more manual labor and less machinery are established in their settlements, it would greatly support employment and increase the income of the poor. May the government pay attention, pay attention, pay attention!
(13:25 hrs)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.
Honourable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:26 hrs)
Sir, when adolescents Sushil Bishwakarma and Barsha Sharma inter-caste married, the final rites for the daughter were performed while she was alive in Bardiya. This is against the law. The maternal relatives had to be taken from the cremation site to jail. A Dalit built a temple and an idol of a deity. When he went to worship, he was banned from entering the temple, and in anger, he said the temple should be set on fire, and Janak Pariyar was arrested by the police. When someone said, "I will burn down Singh Durbar," why was there silence? Whom should be punished? The government should not lose its conscience. Thank you.
Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
(13:27 hrs)
Right Honourable Chairperson: - And
Honourable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepali Communist Party):-
(13:27 hrs)
Mr. Chairperson, the government has been removing the settlements of landless Dalits, squatters, and unorganized residents in various places across the country, including the Kathmandu Valley, since Jestha 12th. This work has not stopped even though the Supreme Court issued an interim order to halt it. 750 families and 16,843 individuals have been forcibly rendered homeless. The government's records show only 10,425 registered, while 6,448 individuals are yet to be registered. Through the Honourable Chairperson, I strongly urge the government to register the remaining individuals immediately. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(13:28 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Mr. Chairperson,
(13:28 hrs)
I want to ask the government what it is doing regarding problem resolution, rising inflation, and the tea industry that has closed or is about to close. Regarding the flawed statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister concerning Nepal-India border relations, and the unlawful, anarchic, and threatening statements made by Honourable Ministers, questions are arising from the public; when will we get answers? Also, what steps is the government taking to facilitate Nepal-India trade relations? I want to ask through the Honourable Chairperson. New petrol, diesel, and EV vehicles also seem to be stopped; what is the reason? If the tendency is to remain intoxicated with populism, at least do not put on a ridiculous show. Finally, I want to assure that considering the mistakes made by us regarding the Alternative Finance Management Bill, the National Assembly will be more responsible and accountable in the future. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Rajendra Lakshmi Gaire.
(13:29 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Rajendra Lakshmi Gaire (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:29 hrs)
Sir, the government started demolishing the settlements of landless Dalits, squatters, and unorganized residents since Jestha 12th. Article 37 of the Constitution of Nepal states that every citizen has the right to housing. Article 38 talks about the rights of women, and Article 40 talks about providing land to Dalits. Why is the government not functioning according to the constitution? Why is it playing games? I want an answer for this. The person living there considers it their home, and that person is working for the country and the people while living there. The government must understand this. Another issue is that the Lumbini entrepreneurs' association in Nepal has raised its voice. Instead of making payments to them, they have been threatened with physical harm in the field. The country cannot run like this; the people are in fear. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(13:30 hrs)
(Nepali Communist Party):-
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar
(13:30 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson, we members of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly are a disgrace, let alone honourable. I want to raise a few points regarding the inconsistent and security policy that favors the wealthy and affluent, which is in place for members entering the main west gate of Singh Durbar. If one arrives in their car or private vehicle, the security personnel allow them to enter freely. If they come on foot, they are not allowed. Sometimes they are allowed, sometimes not. One must wear a logo, show a pass. Why such an inconsistent policy?
I want to raise this one point. Another thing is, if it's for security reasons, then wouldn't it be more insecure in a car? Bombs and explosives could be brought in a car, right? An individual probably cannot. Therefore, the concerned authorities should formulate a correct, alternative policy. I am also against this. That's why I raised this issue.
Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the order of speaking during the Zero Hour
(13:31 hrs)
concludes here. Honourable members, names have been received on a party basis for speaking during the Provincial Concerns Hour. Now, I will provide time to the Honourable members in order. First, Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra, time 12 minutes. After that, Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson,
(13:32 hrs)
Respected Honourable members, especially concerning the budget prepared by this government for the Sudurpashchim Province today, Dhanagadhi bazaar, which is currently operating as the capital of Sudurpashchim. During his visit to India, the Right Honourable former Prime Minister, respected Sher Bahadur Deua, had reached an agreement to make Ghuariphanta a cross-border international checkpoint under point number 35. If that Ghuariphanta checkpoint is not used as an international checkpoint, my respected brothers will develop here on the basis of equality and equitable budget distribution. However, looking at the size of the budget, it appears neither balanced nor equitable. Therefore, the issue is that if development is not distributed across all sectors, it cannot be called development. My request is, there are numerous problems. Sometimes it is said there is Chhaupadi in Sudurpashchim, sometimes the issue of Kamaiya is raised, sometimes the issue of Kamlari is raised. Problems are raised at the national level, but solutions are not sought. The people of Sudurpashchim, who are waiting with hope for justice from the new government with new enthusiasm, are the Honourable Ministers of the government here today. I want to ask, have you delivered justice? Is this justice? Therefore, there are numerous opportunities. It's not just about the Ghuariphanta checkpoint. There are tourist attractions...

There are places. Big places where development can be done, where tourism can be brought. From the Gawari Phanta border crossing, there is a place called Khandada. While it is 41-42 degrees Celsius in the heat below, if you go up, you get a cool 18-19-20 degrees Celsius. And today, to showcase all these tourists, to add all dimensions of development, no steps are being taken. Is this what the new government and the people expected when they voted for you?

Not only that, today the cities to the south, with their historical names like Satti, Bhajani, Rajapur, were reduced to ashes due to the highway. But as the Hulaki highway began to revive them a little, the road from section number 3 of the Hulaki road to Khakhola in Tikapur has been in a state where it cannot be traversed due to floods for 5-6 years now. That road has not been repaired. Whether we talk about Khaptad, Ramaroshan, or Badimalika, it is not appropriate to neglect such important places. That is why this is stuck. Is this government's behavior towards the Sudurpaschim Province, which was once envisioned as the new state of Banke, Bardia, Kailali, Kanchanpur? Therefore, I want to say, if you cannot deliver justice, justice is not something that anyone else will give or take. The people there will seek justice themselves if you neglect them. Therefore, it is the responsibility of this state to care for every region; it is not for any individual to give or take. I humbly request that the government's attention be turned towards Sudurpaschim Province. I request that the mistakes made be corrected.

Furthermore, there is great arrogance visible in our government today. It is very strange. The honorable Prime Minister talks about tying someone to a tree. Ministers talk about breaking legs, and some say India is encroaching on Nepal's land. There is no logic, no meaning. Whatever comes to their mouths, they say. Is this state run by constitution, law, procedure, and system? My question is. Are people talking about 21st-century technology today, and is this government, the Rastriya Swatantra Party government, moving towards making a village chief in every village, and that chief's directives becoming the law and rule? My question is. Therefore, I humbly request all of you. A narrative is being created these days. I humbly request all the honorable ministers of the Rastriya Swatantra Party, who are 34 years old. If those from 35 years ago had not done something, perhaps you would not be honorable ministers and Prime Minister today. If it is the people from 35 years ago who ruined things, then I have a question for you. Those from 35 years ago, whether they were our mothers, fathers, grandparents, or any relation, some might have been in politics, some in jobs, some in contracting. They were in their respective work and professions. If the property of the new is not investigated, and only the old is investigated, then I humbly request all my honorable ministers from here: let's start with your own fathers and grandfathers first, then with us. The law does not distinguish between new and old. Is it just for new people to be exempt from any law, while old people are brought under money laundering? Is this state trying to divide into new and old, or is it trying to run the state according to just and constitutional arrangements? My question is. Therefore, the point is that public opinion is not that important. Fulfill the promises you have made to the public, and I wish the Rastriya Swatantra Party government a 20-year term. If you have the arrogance that whatever we say will be implemented, that we don't need laws, we don't need a constitution, we don't need rules, then be warned. Ram was born for Ravana. Therefore, someone will be born. If all old things are useless, then I want to recall the events of the 23rd and 24th. Do we need the parliament, the Supreme Court, the police, and are the offices we have destroyed all necessary? This knowledge is lacking. Therefore, individuals can be bad... Physical structures may not be bad. We honorable members sitting here may have shortcomings, but this chair and this hall have no shortcomings, if there is consciousness. Therefore, new is not green and yellow. For the new, if you think you will be kings by destroying the contractors, the country's employees, trade unions, student organizations, and everything today with your arrogance, then I humbly request that you are mistaken. A child who has woken up in the dark cannot find the way; you are in that state.

I humbly request one more thing. If all old things are bad, then from where did you become good, having entered the system that came from the old? Did you come from some other world? Were you born in Nepal? Are you Nepali? My question is. You must not have come from some other world. This is the society, this is the environment. We are someone's brother, someone's son. Therefore, the natural principle does not state that only what I do is beautiful and what others do is bad. If nature is considered... when nature changes its form, no scientist can stop the suffering that nature inflicts on the people of this earth, like earthquakes. If you remember, today everything is invented, but scientists cannot stop earthquakes, floods, rain, or sunshine. My honorable colleague is also present in that subject.

Therefore, speaking baseless things is like spitting upwards at the sky; think about the consequences. If you abuse the old, belittle them, and say they did nothing, then if you do not accept the existence of others, your own existence has no justification. Keeping all this in mind, I request you all and end my speech. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima", (1:43 PM) Time 10 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal):- (1:43 PM) Honorable Chairperson, on the evening of Jestha 28th, around 8 PM, a very tragic and sensitive incident occurred in Balata, Ward No. 4 of Dhakari Rural Municipality in Achham District. When local people's representative, Ward Member Manisha Saud, suddenly had abdominal pain, she requested her relatives and Dharmaraj Saud of the same ward to bring medicine. Since Dharmaraj Saud could not send anyone else, he went to her house with the medicine himself. However, shortly after he reached the house, some local individuals, without any factual basis or evidence, accused them of having an illicit relationship and beat them up. Not only that, they filmed the incident and widely publicized it on social media, attempting to tarnish their character. Despite both individuals repeatedly clarifying that they had no such relationship and that he had only come to deliver medicine, the accusers did not listen. Both were severely beaten. After the incident, Manisha Saud became a victim of severe mental stress, humiliation, and social stigma. She went out of contact from Jestha 29th and her body was found three days later on Jestha 31st. I am heartbroken by this tragic news. I offer my deepest condolences to the deceased Manisha Saud and express my sympathy to her family. Accusing someone without understanding the reality, beating them publicly, making videos to tarnish their character on social media, and creating an environment of social humiliation is extremely reprehensible and against the law. The serious question before society and the state today is whether such activities have mentally weakened an innocent person to the point that she had to lose her life. Therefore, I demand that all individuals involved in this incident be impartially investigated. I demand that all those directly or indirectly involved in beating, filming, broadcasting on social media, and defaming be brought to justice and severely punished. Furthermore, it is a shameful matter that women have to be afraid to speak to anyone, seek help, or maintain social relationships. In the 21st century, such thinking and behavior that question the freedom, dignity, and social existence of women in a democratic society must end. Honorable Chairperson, Manisha Saud was a ward member. I wish to draw the government's serious attention to the expectation that no woman, even one holding a responsible position like a people's representative, should have to lose her life due to humiliation and inferiority complex in the future. Honorable Chairperson, now I would like to say a few words about federalism. Federalism is the division and adjustment of state power and responsibilities between two or more levels of government. Federalism divides political, economic, and administrative power and responsibilities among different levels of government. In essence, federal governance systems are formed through two processes. First, federalism formed by the union of independent states, for example, the United States of America and Switzerland. Second, countries with a unitary system of government adopting a federal system, like Nepal and South Africa. We brought federalism after long struggles and sacrifices to establish unity in diversity, manage conflict, protect local identity, utilize local opportunities, preserve identity, ensure ownership of all classes in the state, and for political participation and development. Just as a child needs to be nurtured after birth, that nurturing has not happened. In general principle, the weak need more care. They need more nurturing. In accordance with this principle, the central government has not looked after Sudurpaschim, Karnali, and Madhesh as it should have. Looking at the nature of budget allocation, this budget allocation is contrary to the spirit and letter of federalism.

Honorable Chairperson, Sudurpaschim's internal revenue collection capacity is comparatively weak. The province's budget is largely dependent on financial transfers from the federal government. Instead of increasing the amount of financial transfer, it has been reduced. Administrative federalism, financial federalism, and political federalism are dimensions of federalism. However, these aspects, these dimensions, have been ignored. Furthermore, the fact that the province's total budget is only about 14 percent of the federal budget shows that a large share of financial resources and authority still lies with the center. And then it is said, the province did not work, it is not the province's job.

Regarding the implementation of federalism, ambiguity in jurisdiction still exists. There is still a lack of federal laws for the implementation of federalism. Administrative authority is lacking. Financial federalism is extremely weak due to a fair lack of grants. There is ambiguity in the management of provincial resources. There is a lack of coordination in inter-governmental relations. And how will the provinces work? Honorable Chairperson, it seems to me that a game is being played to remove the 10-year-old republic and federalism from the race, saying it cannot run. Federalism cannot be strengthened by centralizing power. The republic born after long labor pains...

It is being done in a way that weakens and destroys federalism. This is unacceptable. Honorable Chairperson, the anti-poor government is causing destruction everywhere with the support of power. In Kathmandu, it is boasting about its bravery by demolishing houses and making poor Nepali citizens homeless. The anti-poor government, devoid of empathy, has deprived 37 percent of children of education, plunging their future into darkness. 93 percent of women are suffering from illness and sorrow in holding centers, living in fear of being evicted any day. Seven people have already died. I say to this government, how can you boast about how wonderfully you worked by displacing poor Chameli? How can you be proud of making the lives of poor Nepali citizens miserable by using bulldozers? Schools are closed. Medicine for the sick is unavailable. Stoves for heating water are gone. Warm beds are gone. Families are separated. Instead of providing roofs to the homeless, their roofs have been taken away. The government of the people is nowhere to be found. It is not providing data to show less data of displaced people. The government, which rejoices in the suffering of the poor, is not satisfied with this. In Godavari Municipality of Kailali, Dhana Dhami, who used to sell goods by loading them onto a tempo, has committed the crime of having her tempo confiscated in the name of encroaching on forest land. It has thrown stones at the shacks of the poor and demolished them. I strongly condemn such inhumane, illegal, and unconstitutional actions. Honorable Chairperson, I once read that those who do such things are called robbers. Chairperson, ministers themselves threaten to break bones. When the rulers themselves become anarchic, anarchy begins to be born in the minds of the people. Anarchy begins to gain ground. Did the Nepali people elect Kumar Thapa with a two-thirds majority to commit the murder of his own wife, Indhira Bhujel? In Dhangadhi, Rastra Swatantra Party leader Shailesh Singh is attacked with acid. Did the Nepali people elect with a two-thirds majority to cause chaos, murder, violence, and oppression of the poor? This is my serious question to the government through the Honorable Chairperson. Honorable Chairperson, this government seems like a bundle of lies, a bundle of deceit, a bundle of falsehoods. Before the election, we said that after our strength is sufficient, we will abolish the provinces. While going to the election, we said we would strengthen the provinces, and now when the budget comes, neither have they been abolished nor have they been strengthened. Before the election, we said we would go to the streets of foreign countries, put up posters, and appeal to the emigrated youth to return home and contribute to nation-building. After the election, they send passports to every house. What are passports for? They are for going abroad, aren't they? Before the election, they talked big about nationalism by displaying a Greater Nepal map. Now they seem to be struggling to hide that Greater Nepal map. The current government is being strangled by its past promises. That is why, perhaps, none of the honorable members of the ruling party are seen in the audience today. Perhaps it is due to this fear. Perhaps this is why they are hiding. I would like to request the government through the Honorable Chairperson. This is a golden opportunity. It is a historic opportunity. Utilize it. I conclude with the expectation that you will use it to win the hearts of the people and build the nation in favor of the people. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Prem Prasad Dahal, time 5 minutes. (1:54 PM) After this, Honorable member Mohammad Khalid. Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- (1:54 PM) Honorable Chairperson, today we are discussing and interacting on issues of provincial concern. Although there are many issues regarding whether to keep provinces or not, regarding the form of provinces, their jurisdiction, and also issues of coordination not happening in national politics between inter-provincial, provincial and local levels, and provinces and the center, have all become public. The constitution has directed us to adopt a federal democratic republican governance system with seven provinces. We are in that practice. But the unfortunate thing is that we have not been able to practice this as envisioned by the constitution through the provinces. As a result, it has become a subject of criticism that the service delivery that should have been provided by the provincial governments has not been effective. What could be the reasons for this? Regarding exclusive rights, the respective bodies, i.e., provinces and local levels, are making laws and regulations on their own. As far as the concurrent list is concerned, the making of laws and regulations are issues that have been raised repeatedly in national politics. These issues have been raised and discussed at various levels. Nothing is particularly new. However, I want to emphasize these issues through this assembly. Specifically, the issue of police adjustment has not happened yet. Even though the adjustment act has come, the matter of transferring the police, the matter of transferring them to the provinces, has not happened. Even now, provinces cannot be self-reliant in the budget. The lack of certainty in the ceiling of fiscal equalization grants is one issue. Similarly, in matters like revenue sharing grants, there is a situation where one has to look to others. Similarly, issues within the provincial jurisdiction such as forest use, water use, and mineral exploration, as defined and guided by the constitution, have not been systematically managed to make the provinces economically self-reliant. Similarly, the inability to send employees to the provinces is also a reason. Firstly, there is a mentality among the employees themselves not to want to go to the provinces, to want to stay in the center, and not to want to go to the provinces and local levels. Secondly, the state has not been able to manage the employees accordingly to fulfill the O&M surveys and positions created for provinces, federal government, and local levels. There is a situation where employees cannot be sent to the provinces, and even if they are sent, they are recalled immediately. This issue also needs to be addressed. Similarly, the issue of land acquisition is pending when provinces operate provincial-level projects or establish offices. It has been obstructed many times. This issue also needs to be resolved. Another important issue is our, all of us, centralized mentality; we still have a centralized mentality. I have not seen the physical infrastructure and other projects for this year, but looking at the past, small fragmented projects, whether they are worth one lakh, two lakhs, five lakhs, ten lakhs, or one crore, are still being managed from the center. We urgently need to transfer this to the local bodies and provinces. Our central mentality is that we have to conduct training, we have to manage the market, we have to do small tasks. This is the situation we see. Specifically, I believe we should focus on coordination, facilitation, resource management, monitoring, and motivating provinces and local levels. From the center, we should operate large-scale projects that increase production, productivity, poverty alleviation, and job creation, including national pride projects. Finally, specifically on how to effectively implement the federal, provincial, and local levels, a special committee has been formed in the National Assembly regarding this work. The report of the special committee on the implementation of federalism should be implemented, I believe. Thank you. Namaste. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Mohammad Khalid, time 5 minutes. (1:59 PM) After this, Honorable member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (Janasamajwadi Party, Nepal):- (2:00 PM) Honorable Chairperson, as per the provisions of the National Assembly Rules, we have a provision to speak once a month on provincial concerns and related issues. I would like to thank the Honorable Chairperson for giving me time accordingly. Federalism was established by the constitution of 2072 BS. However, the past decade, from 2072 to 2082 BS, and its practices show that federalism has never been fully realized or digested, and various governments have not worked towards it in their respective times. Leaders said, and we accepted federalism in haste. It has become a burden for this country. That is why the former Chief Minister of our Madhesh Province, Honorable Lalbabu Raut, told the then Prime Minister that "We got the seat, but not the governance." What is needed today is that the current government should consider this and focus on the implementation of federalism. The failure to enact laws on matters of concurrent rights listed in Schedule 7 of the constitution is also a failure of federalism, or a cause, whatever you call it. Similarly, Schedule 6 of the constitution for provinces and Schedule 8 for local levels have been neglected by both provinces and local levels. The center did not manage employees in time. We continuously hear complaints about insufficient budget. This year too, the budget that the provinces have received is slightly more than before, but considering the size of the GDP and the corresponding budget, it is not much. It is not that it has increased, but that it has been received. Police adjustment is an important issue. What kind of government is it without police? The important thing is that I want to raise an issue of provincial concern, and through the Honorable Chairperson, I want this matter to reach the provinces. Whenever we talk about inclusivity and proportionality in accordance with the constitution, we do so. During the appointment of ambassadors, and other political appointments, the voice from below is that it is not proportional. But when it comes to the rulers of the provinces, the provincial governments, when this matter comes to them, they do not consider it. I can say with data that they are proceeding by forgetting these fundamental aspects of the constitution in most matters. Whether it is government formation, political appointments, appointments in various bodies, access to resources, and ensuring that the resources and targeted groups in the provinces reach various castes, communities, and backward classes, the provinces are failing. Provincial governments are failing. If the center makes any mistake, we raise our voice in the National Assembly. It is also raised in the provinces. It is also raised from the local levels. But if the province makes the same mistake, that issue does not come up from anywhere. This is completely wrong. Through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to convey this matter specifically to the provinces, especially to Madhesh Province. Thank you. (2:01 PM) Presiding Officer: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Lila Kumari Bhandari. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota, time 12 minutes. (2:04 PM) Honorable Mr. Vishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, Nepal is not only the birthplace of the universally recognized pioneer of truth and peace, but it also carries the glorious history of Nepal, a mixture of mountains, hills, and plains, all castes, languages, arts, traditions, and cultures, with their own identities in 12 districts.

I consider myself very fortunate to have the opportunity to speak about the Lumbini Province, which has been formed through collaboration. Respected Chairperson, Lumbini Province has 12 districts, 109 local levels, 4 sub-metropolitan cities, 32 municipalities, and 73 rural municipalities. The major rivers in this province include Rapti, Babai, Rohini, Kaligandaki, Purvi Sima Kshetra, Badigad, Tinau, and about 12 others, along with thousands of tributaries and seasonal streams. These offer immense potential for electricity generation. Currently, 21.2 megawatts of electricity are produced, according to data, which includes hydropower and some solar energy projects. Recent studies and research indicate a strong potential for 2.677 megawatts of hydropower generation, with a significant portion still requiring research and development. Honorable Shri Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable

(15:45 hrs)

Mr. Chairperson, as per Rule 89 of Chapter 13 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I seek permission to present a proposal in this esteemed house to reject the ordinance to amend the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2064, among the eight ordinances presented by the government in the house on Jestha 28.

I wish to present some reasons for rejecting the ordinance. On Jestha 17, after a cabinet meeting, a decision was made to convene a parliamentary session, and within 24 hours, the government again postponed the parliament and brought 122 laws amended through eight ordinances. Is it a democratic value and procedural practice to bypass the sovereign parliament of the country and resort to ordinances?

Yes, Article 114 of the Constitution does grant the authority to issue ordinances. However, it appears that the ordinance is being used as a political tool to circumvent parliament, rather than as an emergency provision granted by the constitution, especially when the government has a clear majority.

Mr. Chairperson, I would like to remind you that honorable members who vehemently opposed ordinances while in the opposition benches yesterday have suddenly changed their stance upon assuming power today. Is it the nature of power to repeat the same mistakes made by the previous government, which they themselves pointed out, and to forget the values they themselves established?

If this ordinance, presented in the house on Jestha 28, had been brought through the regular parliamentary process, then considering the time elapsed, there could have been clause-by-clause discussions in the house, and an environment could have been created for all parties and stakeholders to engage in extensive deliberation and collective ownership. When clause-by-clause discussions are not held, the flaws in the laws tend to persist. As a result, such immature laws, when they reach the implementation stage tomorrow, become extremely complex and controversial.

Mr. Chairperson, laws made in the absence of clause-by-clause deliberation in the legislature become extremely complex, controversial, and ineffective in the long run when they reach the implementation stage. Therefore, disregarding the legal principle that process determines the validity of the outcome, I wish to draw the attention of the house to two specific issues in the ordinances brought forth. Money laundering is a commitment to international standards and financial governance. However, serious flaws are evident in this ordinance. One flaw is the duplication of jurisdiction, where sub-clause (c) of clause 13(1) creates a conflict of jurisdiction between the Revenue Investigation Department, Customs, and the Anti-Money Laundering Department. Ambiguity in the law can provide criminals with an escape route from court by taking advantage of technical loopholes.

The second is clause 29(1)(a), which allows for prosecution if the predicate offense is proven...

The arbitrary power has been given to the department. This spreads fear among the private sector and investors and also increases the risk of double punishment. Therefore, Mr. Speaker, I have submitted this motion of dissent not out of personal or party interest, but keeping in mind the public interest, the values of democracy, public expectations, the spirit of the constitution, and the need for good governance. Therefore, I expect one more thing from this respected house: I am confident that this house will make a positive decision on the motion of dissent that I have presented. Mr. Speaker, the ordinance should not always be a hindrance, but a respected house like the National Assembly cannot be a witness to immature and flawed laws. Therefore, I strongly demand that these ordinances be immediately repealed and reviewed, and brought back to the parliament as a general bill for detailed discussion, instead of being passed as they are. Thank you.

Honorable Speaker: Now, I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion on the motion to reject the "Prevention of Money Laundering (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2083 BS".

Honorable Minister of Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle: Honorable Speaker, I have listened carefully and reflected on the comments made by the Honorable Member regarding the ordinance to amend the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2064 BS. The Honorable Member has expressed their views from two angles. First angle: Why was this ordinance necessary? It is true that there was a strong government, and the bill could have been advanced through discussion with sufficient time. However, bringing it as an ordinance, does it infringe upon the democratic spirit? Regarding this view, as the Honorable Member is aware, and as everyone knows, this is not the first time an ordinance has been promulgated in Nepal's constitutional history. The main thing is that we must look at the intention. Was it brought to establish good governance and advance the country, or was it brought to sow the seeds of misgovernance by misusing ordinances as in the past? If we can distinguish between these, we can focus on the merits of the law.

In the past, ordinances were brought to split parties, dissolve parliament, and make things easier for land mafias, drawing widespread criticism. They were brought to circumvent parliamentary scrutiny. This time, the ordinance has been brought to advance the country, and because following the parliamentary process would take time, and we had a sense of urgency to work on this, we decided to proceed through the channel of an ordinance. Taking the parliamentary channel would take two to three months. Since the government, which has received such a massive mandate, does not have the luxury of waiting for that long, we adopted that path. However, it cannot be accepted that this infringes upon the democratic spirit, because the provision envisioned by the constitution itself is not undemocratic or unconstitutional. Ultimately, it has to face parliament, and a replacement bill will come, on which further discussions will be held. However, I would like to argue that the provision brought by the government, based on Article 114 of the constitution, should not be considered otherwise, and its true test lies in its intention. It is important to clarify whether it has been brought to advance the country, for progress, or for regression.

I welcome the substantive points raised by the Honorable Member from the second angle. I also believe that the concerns and worries expressed are valid. The concern that if there is duplication of authority, and the Department of Money Laundering investigates the same case, and the concerned bodies also investigate related offenses, there is a risk that the cases may become weak or the prosecution may become weak because two bodies are investigating in two different places. I welcome this view. The intention here is that if we do not take prompt action on money laundering, the country has gone to the "grey list." It has been about a year and a half since we have been under increased scrutiny of jurisdiction, commonly known as the "grey list." Many restrictions have already begun. If we cannot get out of this in another year or a year and a half, we will go to the "black list," and for a country dependent on such remittances and foreign capital inflow, going to the black list is almost equivalent to being forced to sever ties with the global economy. Countries like Somalia, Haiti, and Iran, which are cut off from the global economy and cannot engage in any business, attract no investment, and tourists are also suspicious – our country will go to such a dire and terrifying situation if we do not act in time. A few weeks ago, high-ranking officials from the FATF (Financial Action Task Force) visited us and consulted with us, and we committed that we will do whatever it takes to get out of this grey list, making a high-level commitment. The leadership for the process of getting out of this overall grey list will be under the Honorable Prime Minister and the Minister of Finance. We have already committed to advancing this campaign with the highest priority, not under the leadership of departmental employees, but under the highest political leadership. Since there is a commitment to action, and in that spirit, legislative commitment is also needed. To reflect that sense of urgency and action, we brought the ordinance at that time. The added subject matter is related to very serious crimes. Smuggling, customs, excise duty, and other taxes, including direct and indirect taxes. Market manipulation, insider trading, and related issues in the securities and commodities market, banking, financial, foreign exchange, negotiable instruments, and insurance-related offenses. The investigation and prosecution of money laundering related to these offenses are intended to be made more effective. This has become even more relevant now, as a case of embezzlement of a huge sum of one hundred and eleven billion rupees (111 billion) has recently been registered in Nepal's financial history. This is a complex, serious, and grave financial crime, where the proceeds from predicate offenses have been laundered and moved towards money laundering. In light of such financial crimes, we have found it necessary to bring this ordinance to take decisive steps.

I have also accepted the points raised by the Honorable Members regarding clause-by-clause discussion. If there are any duplications, ambiguities, uncertainties, or conflicts, the Nepal government is ready to correct them in the replacement bill. For now, I humbly request the Honorable Members to consider the gravity of this matter and accept the presented ordinance. Thank you.
